name: Conditional resting microfilm
summary: A hypothetical simple cellular sheet. A compatible solvent and energy supply are unverified prerequisites; active survival is not established.

morphology.size: A submillimetre sheet, proposed rather than observed.
morphology.bodyPlan: A thin connected layer with little vertical support.
morphology.locomotion: No whole-body locomotion; a low movement budget.
morphology.surfaceCovering: A repairable outer layer, with its protective value conditional on radiation exposure.
morphology.sensorySystems: Local thermal response regulating activity; no image-forming eyes.

adaptations.consequence: Moving and supporting mass requires energy.
adaptations.adaptation: A small flat sheet without whole-body locomotion.
adaptations.reasoning: A low support and movement budget is compatible with the supplied gravity; it sacrifices relocation.

adaptations.consequence: If actual conditions are cold, active chemistry could be limited.
adaptations.adaptation: Local thermal sensing regulates reversible quiescence.
adaptations.reasoning: Reduced activity could conserve resources during cold intervals; it does not establish survival or imply that surface temperature equals equilibrium temperature.

adaptations.consequence: If radiation exposure is significant, chemical damage could occur.
adaptations.adaptation: A repairable outer cell layer provides limited protection.
adaptations.reasoning: If the unknown exposure warrants it, renewing this layer may reduce damage at an energetic cost; no radiation dose or invulnerability is claimed.

survivalStrategy: A low-movement sheet with thermally regulated activity and conditional protection. Solvent and energy availability remain unverified; quiescence offers no guarantee of survival.
